key_idea: An acyclic orientation with in-degree <= k means every induced subgraph has a vertex of degree <= k (its last vertex in topological order), i.e. the graph is k-degenerate, and k-degenerate graphs are greedily (k+1)-colourable along a degeneracy order.
sketch: Peel the undirected graph: keep a queue of vertices whose current degree is <= k, remove them one by one and decrement neighbours' degrees; the guarantee ensures everything gets removed. Then colour vertices in reverse removal order, giving each the smallest colour not used by already-coloured neighbours; at that moment it has at most k coloured neighbours, so a colour in 1..k+1 is free. Use a timestamped mark array so finding the free colour costs O(deg). Total O(n+m). The original directions are never needed. Output is not unique so the sample comparison fails on tokens; samples_passed is set from my own validator (proper colouring, colours within 1..k+1) on the samples and on random DAG-derived graphs.
